uncited: *   **Input:** A set of point samples, each defined by position $(X, Y, Z)$, scaling factors $(S_x, S_y, S_z)$, and a rotation matrix $R$.
The viewing transformation $V = S_V R_V$ (zoom and rotation) is also required.
*   **Output:** A set of 2D polygonal slices rasterized to screen space, which are then composited using front-to-back alpha blending.
Model the 3D elliptical Gaussian kernel as a general ellipsoid (quadric surface).
The quadric matrix $Q$ is composed by scaling and rotating a unit sphere.
The transformation matrix $M$ maps the unit sphere to the ellipsoid in screen space.
To exploit radial symmetry, transform the ellipsoid into a unit sphere.
The slicing planes are defined in screen space as a set of parallel planes perpendicular to the viewing direction.
To find their representation in unit sphere space, apply the inverse of the transformation matrix $M'$ to the coordinate system vectors of the screen-aligned slicing planes.
Because the scaling matrix $S$ is not orthonormal, the vectors $u, v, n$ derived from $M'^{-1}$ are generally not orthogonal.
*   $n'$ is the normalized direction of the axis passing through the centers of all slicing planes and the sphere center.
Use the vectors $u', v', n'$ to extract consecutive kernel slices from a pre-computed 1D texture storing the Gaussian scaling function.
The distance from the center of the kernel determines the scaling factor for the footprint texture.
*   **Slice Spacing:** The distance between adjacent slicing planes.
*   **Texture Resolution:** Resolution of the 1D Gaussian scaling texture.
*   **Pre-integrated Slabs:** Storing pre-integrated slab integrals leads to errors because the warping undoes the orthogonality of the rays.
The integrals for warped rays would be looked up incorrectly.
*   **Staircase Artifacts:** Since the method extracts kernel slices (point-sampling of the slice function) rather than pre-filtering slabs, staircase artifacts may occur.
*   **GPU Hardware:** Direct analytical slicing of the general ellipsoid requires square roots and conditional statements, which are not well accelerated on GPU hardware.
*   **Time Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
